questions.question: In corrupt_spans, what role does <extra_id_0> play in the returned source and target?
options: It replaces every masked token separately, one sentinel per token
It is a normal vocabulary word copied into both sequences
It marks the first masked span in the source and starts that span's original tokens in the decoder target
It marks the end of the entire target but never appears in the source
questions.explanation: Each ordered masked span gets a sentinel in source; target repeats that sentinel and then emits the span's original tokens.

questions.question: Why does the T5 target end with sentinel(len(ordered))?
options: It replaces the first sentinel when spans overlap
It forces the decoder to predict one extra word from the input
It records the number of unmasked tokens in the source
It provides a closing marker after the final recovered span, with no tokens following it
questions.explanation: round_trip treats the last sentinel as a marker with an empty following span, so it closes the target sequence.

questions.question: What does round_trip(source, target) do with a sentinel found in source?
options: It replaces the sentinel with the token span mapped to that sentinel in target
It deletes the sentinel and leaves the missing text absent
It replaces every sentinel with the whole target sequence
It samples a new span from the vocabulary
questions.explanation: The target is parsed into a sentinel-to-span dictionary, and source sentinels are expanded from that dictionary.

questions.question: How does BART text_infill represent a masked span of several tokens?
options: It emits one <mask> token for every removed token
It emits one <mask> token while advancing over the whole span
It deletes the span without leaving any marker
It replaces the span with a T5 <extra_id_0> and its original text
questions.explanation: text_infill appends one mask_token and increments i by span_len; the decoder must infer how many tokens were removed.

questions.question: What does token_delete(tokens, rate=0.15, rng=...) return?
options: The original list sorted by token ID
A same-length list with deleted entries replaced by <mask>
A shorter list containing only tokens whose random draw is at least the deletion rate
One sentinel followed by all deleted tokens
questions.explanation: The list comprehension keeps each token when rng.random() >= rate and emits nothing for the deleted positions.

questions.question: Why are sentence_permute and document_rotate useful as denoising tasks?
options: They reduce every document to its first sentence for classification
They convert every sentence into a bag of unrelated vocabulary IDs
They mask only special tokens so no language modeling is needed
They corrupt order while preserving the token content, giving an encoder-decoder model a reconstruction problem
questions.explanation: Both functions retain the same words but perturb sentence or document order, so the model must learn to restore coherent structure.
